Map PSGC codes to a target release

map_psgc.Rd

Map PSGC codes to a target release

Usage

map_psgc(code, from = "auto", to = latest_release(), changes_only = FALSE)

Arguments

code

A character vector of PSGC codes (10 digits; 9 for codes from `"Q2_2021"`).

from

Release the codes come from, or `"auto"` (default) to detect automatically using the earliest release that contains each code.

to

Target release name. Defaults to [latest_release()].

changes_only

Logical. If `TRUE`, only rows where the code actually changed (i.e. `mapping_type` is not `"direct"`) are returned. Codes that remained unchanged across all hops are dropped. Defaults to `FALSE`.

Value

A data frame with columns `old_code`, `new_code` (`NA` for abolished codes), `mapping_type` (`"direct"`, `"renumbered"`, `"split"`, or `"abolished"`), `from_release`, and `to_release`. A split code produces one row per successor.

Examples

map_psgc("0100000000")
#>     old_code   new_code mapping_type from_release to_release
#> 1 0100000000 0100000000       direct      Q1_2023    Q3_2026
map_psgc(c("0100000000", "0102800000"), to = "Q4_2023")
#>     old_code   new_code mapping_type from_release to_release
#> 1 0100000000 0100000000       direct      Q1_2023    Q4_2023
#> 2 0102800000 0102800000       direct      Q1_2023    Q4_2023
map_psgc(get_psgc("Q1_2023", geographic_level = "Bgy")$psgc_code,
         from = "Q1_2023", to = "Q4_2023", changes_only = TRUE)
#>      old_code   new_code mapping_type from_release to_release
#> 1  0402103001       <NA>    abolished      Q1_2023    Q4_2023
